key_insight: Apply a multi-head low-rank factorization to the KV cache so you keep the small cache size of latent-attention methods while avoiding the tensor-parallel sharding bottleneck—enabling much cheaper, scalable long-context decoding.
problem_solved: Decoding with long contexts is limited by repeated KV cache transfers from off-chip HBM to on-chip SRAM and by a sharding/communication bottleneck when using Tensor Parallelism.
method: Introduce a multi-head low-rank attention representation that compresses per-head K/V information without breaking tensor-parallel sharding patterns.
Design cache layout and decomposition so each TP shard can load and use a small on-chip low-rank KV factor locally, removing cross-shard dependencies during generation.
Hardware-aware choices (rank, layout, and quantization) to balance accuracy, on-chip SRAM footprint, and off-chip bandwidth.
impact: Enables faster, more memory- and bandwidth-efficient long-context inference for LLMs in both single-node and distributed setups—reducing latency and HBM traffic while scaling with TP. Practitioners can handle longer contexts or larger models without proportional increases in memory bandwidth or decoding time.
visual_elements: Before vs After diagram: full KV cache transfers per step (many HBM→SRAM moves) vs low-rank per-head factors loaded once or less frequently.
Distributed decoding schematic: show tensor-parallel shards with MLA (cross-shard communication arrows) vs multi-head low-rank (local-only arrows).
Chart: decoding latency or HBM bandwidth vs context length comparing baseline, MLA, and Multi-Head Low-Rank Attention.
Icon set: KV cache (memory), compression/low-rank (matrix with reduced rank), TPU/accelerator shard (chip icons), speed/bandwidth meter.
paper_authors: Songtao Liu, Hongwu Peng, Zhiwei Zhang, Zhengyu Chen, Yue Guo
